label: LTEE Cit+ emergence and Cit++ expansion
summary: Leon et al. (2018) describe emergence of citrate utilization in the Ara−3 LTEE population after 31,500 generations and descendants fully exploiting citrate by 33,000 generations.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

label: CitT duplication fitness in early LTEE Cit+ isolate
summary: Leon et al. (2018) measured a 2.2% competitive fitness advantage associated with the citT-activating duplication by comparing early Cit+ isolate ZDB564 with its Cit− revertant ZDB706.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

label: Weak ancestral fitness benefit of aerobic citT activation
summary: Leon et al. (2018) measured a 1.0% fitness advantage for the engineered Cit+ activation in ancestral LTEE strain REL606, with weak statistical support (one-tailed P = 0.033; n = 12).

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

label: Deleterious citT activation in evolved genetic backgrounds
summary: Leon et al. (2018) reported that activating citT reduced competitive fitness in 11 of 23 tested evolved pre-Cit+ clones, including five with reductions greater than 20%.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

label: Negative Cit+ activation effect in intermediate Ara−3 phylogeny
summary: Leon et al. (2018) estimated a −5.4% fitness effect (interval −7.2% to −3.6%) for citT activation in the intermediate pre-Cit+ lineage group represented by ZDB425, ZDB458 and ZDB464.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

label: Late positive Cit+ activation effect in Ara−3 phylogeny
summary: Leon et al. (2018) estimated a +2.4% fitness effect (95% interval +1.4% to +3.4%) in a later fully potentiated pre-Cit+ lineage group containing ZDB19 and ZDB13 from as early as 29,000 generations.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

label: Ecological potentiation test in evolved generation-31,000 Ara−3 population mixture
summary: Leon et al. (2018) measured a 0.9% Cit+ fitness advantage when competing engineered ZDB706 variants at low frequency within the generation-31,000 LTEE population and reported no support for an ecological-potentiation advantage.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

label: Loss of detectable Cit− lineage in Ara−3 samples
summary: Turner et al. (2015) detected the Ara−3 Cit− genotype and phenotype through 43,500 LTEE generations but not in samples from 44,000 generations onward.

sources.title: Replaying Evolution to Test the Cause of Extinction of One Ecotype in an Experimentally Evolved Population

label: Cit− persisted through 40 reconstructed evolution replays
summary: Turner et al. (2015) found Cit− persistence in all 20 replay populations from generation 43,500 and all 20 from generation 40,000 after 500 generations, plus one generation-43,000 replay propagated for 2,500 generations.

sources.title: Replaying Evolution to Test the Cause of Extinction of One Ecotype in an Experimentally Evolved Population

label: Reinvasion of a 50,000-generation Cit+ population
summary: Turner et al. (2015) observed that a generation-43,000 Cit− clone reinvaded the generation-50,000 Ara−3 population, reaching about 3 × 10^5 cells/mL, roughly an order of magnitude below final Cit− densities in the other treatments.

sources.title: Replaying Evolution to Test the Cause of Extinction of One Ecotype in an Experimentally Evolved Population

label: Turner extinction cause unresolved; random-catastrophe proposal
summary: Turner et al. (2015) stated that the Ara−3 Cit− lineage extinction cause remained unknown, rejected their initial ongoing Cit+ adaptation explanation, and proposed an unidentified rare perturbation as a possible cause rather than an observed event.

sources.title: Replaying Evolution to Test the Cause of Extinction of One Ecotype in an Experimentally Evolved Population
